posts.title: Alert-Sound Reaction
posts.feeling: Sleeping through a national emergency.
posts.line: A bit about his own sleep. Nobody in it to call out but himself, and it sank into the bottom half.

flow.beat: Close-up of a man waking up startled in bed and looking around in confusion.
Loud, exaggerated gasping and heavy breathing play while he sits up quickly, looks distressed, and runs a hand through his hair.
High-pitched emergency siren beeps and a robotic female voice read an alert message while he ducks back down onto the bed and covers his head.

posts.hook: alert notification miss kardiya kyunki mai 2 PM ke pehle nahi uth ta
named: Indian Government Emergency Alert System Test
posts.label: Sleeps through the national emergency alert
posts.take: He sleeps through the nationwide emergency-alert test because he “doesn’t wake up before 2 PM”. Everyone got that alert, so the moment was free, but the reel is just him jolting awake in bed. Nothing for anyone to grab.

posts.title: Split by alarm
posts.feeling: Delhi panics. Mumbai shrugs.
posts.line: A Mumbai-vs-Delhi contrast. It points at another city instead of laughing at his own, and it held the middle.

flow.beat: Close-up of a young man in a white patterned shirt and silver chain; he looks around nervously; on-screen text reads “hearing the alarm: Delhi”; a brief Hindi line is interrupted by an aggressive off-screen male voice.
Single jump cut; the same man faces sideways with a relaxed expression; on-screen text changes to “hearing the alarm: Mumbai”; the audio shifts to soft casual English.

posts.hook: hearing the alarm: Delhi
posts.label: An alarm goes off: Delhi panics, Mumbai shrugs
posts.take: The same guy hears an alarm twice: as a Delhi guy (panic, shouting) and as a Mumbai guy (a shrug). A city stereotype his crowd has seen a hundred times. Middle of the pack.

posts.title: Escalate Then Clap
posts.feeling: Moving in together ruins everything.
posts.line: He plays both flatmates. A general premise with no tribe he belongs to, and it sat low.

flow.beat: Close-up of a young man saying they should move in together; top text reads “How to ruin a friendship immediately.”
Cut to a second character agreeing, then back to the first character agreeing to the plan.
The second character says he drank all the other’s milk; the first character says he has dreams where he slits his throat and watches his parents cremate him.
The second character stares in shocked silence, then both characters perform a rapid hand-slapping and clapping routine.

posts.hook: How to ruin a friendship immediately
posts.label: Two flatmates trade dark confessions
posts.take: He plays two flatmates who decide to move in, then trade confessions (“I drank your milk”, “I dream about my own funeral”) and break into a hand-slap routine. A dark swerve, but nobody in his crowd knows these two guys.

posts.title: Hard Cut to Notification
posts.feeling: “Reels is not a job.”
posts.line: Arjun bhai lectures him, and Zomato’s notification answers back. He is the one being judged here, and this angle keeps landing in the bottom third.

flow.beat: Close-up of a young man speaking to camera in a bedroom; he gestures with pleading expressions.
Spoken Hinglish text addresses “Arjun bhai” and says scrolling reels is not a job, asks to find a job, do something, and ends with “Par maine aisa kyun bola?”
A hard cut lands on a top-down shot of a black iPhone on a bed; a chime plays.
The lock screen shows Fri 1 May, 6:02, and a Zomato notification banner with “You’ve been someone’s reason to smile today 👉👈 Let us be yours 🍛”; a quiet Hindi voiceover plays.

posts.hook: Arjun bhai scrolling reels is not a job bhai.
posts.label: A friend lectures him that reels aren’t a job
posts.take: He lectures “Arjun bhai” that scrolling reels isn’t a job, then a Zomato notification cuts in as the punchline. The joke lives in a phone banner you have to read in a second. And it’s Anuj getting preachy, which his crowd never orders.

posts.title: Replace With AI
posts.feeling: Even an AI is a better son than an influencer.
posts.line: The creator gets replaced by an AI in his own home, and Blinkit saves Mother’s Day. The brand paid for his angle on creators, not for his face, and it is the ceiling of this memory.

flow.beat: Mother asks how to upload on WhatsApp; son says he is a macro influencer and has no time.
A black-turtleneck, star-headband AI character appears and helps her.
Mother asks what to gift for Gauri’s shih tzu; son gives a lazy answer; AI gives pet gift options.
Mother feeds, hugs, and selfies with the AI while the son watches, then bangs on the glass door from outside.
Son chokes the AI; the AI says how to win the mother back.
Blinkit app ordering appears, then a boAt smartwatch is delivered and given to the mother; Mother’s Day text closes the reel.

posts.hook: How do I upload this on whatsapp?
posts.label: Blinkit ad: his mom swaps him for an AI assistant
posts.take: A Blinkit ad, dropped right before Mother’s Day: his mom asks for help with WhatsApp, he’s “too busy being a macro influencer”, so she adopts an AI helper instead, and he has to order her a boAt watch to win her back. A brand deal that is actually a story, on the right weekend. The best-fed reel of the 90 days.

posts.title: Swap MJ Meaning
posts.pokes: The friend who gets it wrong
posts.feeling: That one friend who mixes up every reference.
posts.line: A general friend type, not a tribe he is inside. District shows up only on the end card. Just below the middle.

flow.beat: Two people walk on a paved seaside path with palm trees.
The woman speaks on her phone; the man smiles, reacts, and holds his head.
The woman answers a call from her mother; the transcript includes “GHADE KI AULLAAAD”; the man dances in the background.
Cut to an indoor party space with silver tinsel and a life-sized Michael Jackson cardboard cutout; the man wears a basketball jersey and fedora and holds a basketball; they argue and dance.
They dance in a dim bar with blue and purple lights while holding microphones and singing.
Photo-style cuts show them posing with the Michael Jackson cutout.
They dance with another man dressed as Michael Jackson; the overlay “district FANS ONLY” appears.
Black screen with white text “district movies.”

posts.hook: That one friend who gets everything wrong
posts.label: District ad: a Jordan-or-Jackson mix-up
posts.take: District ad: his friend mixes up Michael Jordan and Michael Jackson on the way to a concert. A one-line joke stretched to a minute, and the brand only appears on the end card.

posts.title: Viralize the clip
posts.feeling: One viral video and suddenly it’s an “IP”.
posts.line: He and Ruhee play the creators he knows: 10 million views, IP talk, can’t pay the cafe bill. He is guilty of it too, which is why it stings. Near the top.

flow.beat: A woman and a man count to five with hand gestures in a living room while “Ek Do Teen” plays.
The man shouts “Chal dhating naach!” and the duo dance across a living room, street, and cafe to “Dhating Naach.”
Outside a cafe, they look at a phone, react to “10 million,” and repeatedly say they will make an “IP.”
Inside the cafe, they pose while a barista points at the payment terminal and asks them to pay.
They pace outside on phone calls, talk about brands, commercials, and budget, then shout together.

posts.hook: Creators after that one VIRAL video
posts.label: Creators after one viral video talk “IP”
posts.take: He and Ruhee Dosani play creators whose one reel hit 10 million. Suddenly it’s an “IP”, there are brand calls, and they still can’t pay the café bill. Every creator watching has met these two, or been them. Top 10%.

posts.title: Force a Hug
posts.speaks: Anyone who has watched a road fight
posts.feeling: Every road fight has one guy who takes charge.
posts.line: He plays the guy who appoints himself mediator, and the Kokilaben-or-“Ambani” line only a Mumbaikar says out loud. Upper third.

flow.beat: Anuj speaks to camera on a night street, then turns to the scooter rider holding his shoulder.
Anuj demonstrates deep breathing; the scooter rider copies him while speaking in pain.
Anuj says he has studied medical and tells the rider to move his arm.
The camera pans to the cab driver by a white car; Anuj tells him to take the injured man to hospital in his AC car.
The cab driver says the scooter rider is also at fault; Anuj interrupts, mentions “blood on your hands,” and the cab driver shows a dent and scratch on the car door.
Anuj says not to fight, mentions Kokilaben, and asks if there is any hospital better than “Ambani.”
Anuj tells them to hug; they hug, then he joins for a three-way hug.

posts.hook: Ek second, ek second, aise situation mein thoda saas lo pehle.
posts.label: He forces a hug at a roadside crash
posts.take: A real roadside fight between a scooter rider and a cab driver. Anuj walks in, makes them do breathing exercises, waves Kokilaben hospital at them and forces a three-way hug. Real strangers make it; at over a minute it runs out of road.

posts.title: Roll and Cut
posts.feeling: “We get it bro.” You bought the car.
posts.line: The BMW arrives already heckled by its own caption. He calls the bluff on his own flex before anyone else can. Upper quarter.

flow.beat: Matte black BMW sedan is parked in a garage bay under warm lights; centered top text reads “we get it bro 🙏”.
The car rolls forward onto a driveway as the camera pans to the front grille and LED headlights.
Close-up shifts to the front-left wheel and headlight, then to a rear shot against a sunset sky with plate “MP4”.
Side panning and tracking shots show the car moving slowly, then passing other parked vehicles; the driver’s door opens slightly.
Rear-angle and close-up shots return to the dual exhaust, rear diffuser, front-left headlight, and wheel.

posts.hook: we get it bro 🙏
posts.label: His new BMW, captioned “we get it bro”
posts.take: First look at his new matte-black BMW, captioned “we get it bro 🙏”. He rolls his eyes at his own flex before you can. That pre-emptive roast is the whole trick. Top quarter.

posts.title: Skip and React
posts.feeling: Editing out the cheating part.
posts.line: A confession about his own night. The camera is on him, and it settled below the middle.

flow.beat: Young man in backseat, talking animatedly, smiling, gesturing left.
Black-and-white filter; he looks down, smiles, and covers his face with his hand.
Return to color and a slightly different angle; he laughs and looks around the car interior.
Original angle and color; he keeps talking, wipes his eye, and gestures while smiling.

posts.hook: when ur telling the girls about last nights story but u gotta skip past the part where u were cheating
posts.label: Retelling a night, skipping the cheating part
posts.take: Telling the girls about last night while skipping the part where he cheated. The guilty bit flashes to black and white. One expression doing all the work, and it isn’t enough.

posts.title: Rig a Boom Battle
posts.feeling: Everyone’s a rapper until the shopkeeper judges.
posts.line: A shopkeeper judges a diss battle at a cosmetics stall. The crowd carries it into the upper half.

flow.beat: Three young men stand in front of a cosmetics stall; the front rapper holds a microphone and phone, and the shopkeeper sits to the right.
The shopkeeper says “Boom” into the microphone.
The bathrobe-wearing rapper delivers a verse, points at the tall man, then passes the microphone back for another “Boom,” with a black-and-white flash.
The sunglasses-wearing rapper takes the microphone, reads from a red notebook, and gets reactions from the others, with another black-and-white flash.
He continues reading; the shopkeeper repeats “Boom,” and the first rapper and shopkeeper do a quick handshake.
The tall rapper steps forward, reads from his phone, and is interrupted and corrected as he struggles with Hindi grammar.
The tall rapper asks who was best; the shopkeeper points to the bathrobe-wearing rapper as winner, and the others protest.

posts.hook: Diss track battle in public 💀
posts.label: A rap battle at a street cosmetics stall
posts.take: A diss-track battle at a roadside cosmetics stall. The shopkeeper says “Boom” after every verse and picks the winner. The shopkeeper steals it; the reel is long enough that most people never meet him.

posts.title: Split Life Updates
posts.feeling: Girls get drama. Boys get a shrug.
posts.line: A gender contrast with no tribe he belongs to. It fell short of seven straight.

flow.beat: Female character with short dark hair looks serious; second female character with a high bun looks concerned.
First female character speaks with intense facial expressions.
Second female character reacts with shock and anger; first female character begins to weep.
Male character with curly hair and bright orange reflective sunglasses smiles and speaks casually.
Bald male character scratches his head, smiles, and gives a casual response.

posts.hook: Guys, so I have to talk to you all about something.
posts.label: Girls’ life updates vs boys’ life updates
posts.take: Girls sharing life updates (big drama, tears) vs boys (a shrug), all played by him in wigs. A premise the internet has done to death.

posts.title: Hands over cash
posts.feeling: The card doesn’t show the angle.
posts.line: Cash handed to a worker on scaffolding. The reader can’t tell who the joke is on, so it stays unexplained.

flow.beat: A young man opens double glass doors and steps onto a balcony.
He leans over the railing and greets a worker on bamboo scaffolding; the worker smiles up.
Close-ups show his hand on the railing, watch, tattoo, and gestures toward the ropes.
He looks down, talks, laughs, and the worker keeps smiling.
He hands several Indian Rupee cash notes to the worker, who accepts them smiling.

posts.hook: Arre bhaiya... haan.
posts.label: He hands cash to a scaffolding worker
posts.take: He leans off his balcony, chats with a worker on the bamboo scaffolding and hands him some cash. Sweet. But there’s no joke and no point of view, so there’s nothing to send to the group chat.

posts.title: Panic-Cut Through Street
posts.feeling: SoBo kids think the world ends at Bombay.
posts.line: A class joke inside Mumbai, told by someone who knows exactly who the SoBo brats are. It beat four straight.

flow.beat: Five young people stand on a city street at night with exaggerated confusion and disbelief.
One man jumps up and down; the group lines up and raises their arms while looking upward.
One man walks around looking lost; another stares wide-eyed into the camera; one man jumps over another’s shoulder.
The group pretends to make frantic phone calls, then runs in a chaotic circle and bumps into one another.

posts.hook: sobo brats finding out that there is a world that exists outside of bombay
posts.label: South Bombay kids lost outside their bubble
posts.take: South Bombay rich kids find out there’s a world outside Bombay and panic on a night street. A very Mumbai jab, played by the whole crew. Just outside his top quarter.

posts.title: Flip whiteboard beats
posts.feeling: One meme, and suddenly it’s an “Italy expansion proposal”.
posts.line: He plays a marketing team milking “Melodi”: whiteboard, cash, robe, toast. The industry he works in, called out from inside. #2 in memory.

flow.beat: man in black Versace bathrobe stands by a black piano, draws a heart on a whiteboard next to “MODI” under a “FLAMES” layout; “MELONY” and “FLAMES” and “MODI” are visible.
cut to a balcony drink, then the man on a grey sofa holding a thick stack of cash to his ear, then slapping his leg with the cash.
cut back to the whiteboard reading “ITALY EXPANSION PROPOSAL,” then the man wipes the board clean with a cloth.
the man sits on the grey sofa and raises a wine glass toward the camera before the cut ends mid-action.

posts.hook: Parle marketing team rn
posts.label: Parody of Parle’s marketing team milking “Melodi”
posts.take: He plays Parle’s marketing team milking the “Melodi” meme (Modi + Meloni): a FLAMES chart on a whiteboard, cash held to his ear like a phone, an “Italy expansion proposal”. The internet was already laughing at that meme; he gave it a boardroom. #2 of 40.

posts.title: Invent a Driver
posts.feeling: Blame someone who doesn’t exist.
posts.line: A self-recorded excuse plan. The joke is on his own scheme, and it held the middle.

flow.beat: Selfie close-up in a bright indoor hallway; he smiles at camera.
He walks through a lobby toward elevators while talking to camera.
In the elevator, he shows a smiling uniformed staff member and laughs while explaining the plan.
He exits into a basement parking garage and speaks loudly to an off-camera attendant.
He gestures, points at parking spots, scratches his head, and keeps naming a “new driver.”
He listens off-camera, sticks out his tongue briefly, nods, and continues the same story.

posts.hook: blame someone that does not exist
posts.label: He blames a parking mess on a made-up driver
posts.take: He gets a parking complaint and blames “the new driver”, who doesn’t exist, all the way down to the basement. A great lie stretched over 90 seconds of hallway.

posts.title: Rapid-fire Answer Check
posts.feeling: No angle. A panel answers questions.
posts.line: A Startup Village panel. The sponsor bought a format, not his viewpoint. Every post before it landed higher.

flow.beat: black-and-white glitch intro shows two men talking; static transition plays.
color footage shows several young men at a white conference table greeting the camera and laughing.
the group answers “IS COLLEGE WORTH IT?” in rapid cuts.
the host asks “CLAUDE CODE OR CODEX?”; one participant says “Cursor,” and two men share a handshake/high-five.
the group answers “WHICH SUBREDDIT DO YOU USE THE MOST?”; subreddit names appear as text overlays.
the group answers “WHAT IS YOUR FAVORITE THING TO DO OUTSIDE OF WORK?”; split-screen shows reactions to “getting lost in jungles” and “mountain climbing in Delhi.”
the host shows screen time on a phone; a split-screen shows two participants reacting.
the participants wave goodbye; the end card shows “STARTUP VILLAGE MUMBAI” and “little unusual” logos.

posts.hook: RAPID FIRE
posts.label: Sponsored Startup Village rapid-fire panel
posts.take: A sponsored Startup Village panel: is college worth it, Claude Code or Codex, favourite subreddits. It’s an event recap with Anuj in it, not an Anuj reel, and his crowd treated it that way. Dead last.

posts.title: Roast the Crowd
posts.feeling: Hosting a roast and losing control of it.
posts.line: Street mic in the Versace robe, ending with him quitting his own show. The middle.

flow.beat: Host in a black Versace bathrobe, sunglasses, and backward cap speaks to onlookers on a night street.
He interacts with a boy in a blue Manchester United jersey, then asks about Aryan Kataria; black-and-white flashes and ding sounds punctuate reactions.
Aryan, in sunglasses with a McDonald's fry box, delivers a rhyming roast; the crowd reacts and the camera shows two girls walking away laughing.
A tall blonde guy takes the mic and delivers a fast Hindi rap roast; the host asks for a winner and the crowd calls names.
The host counts votes, says he does not want to participate anymore, and the video cuts to black.

posts.hook: My name is Anuj and I'm just here for the vibes, boom.
posts.label: A street-mic roast hosted in a bathrobe
posts.take: Street mic in a Versace bathrobe: two kids roast each other, the crowd votes, and he quits his own show. The strangers are funny; the reel is long.

posts.title: Flip into Dad
posts.feeling: Dad thinks your Instagram is a waste.
posts.line: He plays his own dad calling his videos “waahiyat”. The camera turns on his life, and it drops to the bottom quarter.

flow.beat: Medium close-up of a young man in a blue Nike t-shirt smiles, gestures, and holds up a playing card to someone off-camera.
On-screen text reads, “POV: you go to a guys house but his unemployed dad is also there”.
Hard cut to black-and-white. The same actor plays the dad and speaks off-camera to Anuj and the friend.

He delivers mixed English and Hindi lines about money, a bad magician, not giving ₹3000, not listening to his father, not doing engineering or MBA, posting “waahiyat video” on Instagram, calling for the mother, and torn boxers.
He shifts eye-line left and right, rubs his face, covers his eyes with both hands, and laughs at the end.

posts.hook: POV: you go to a guys house but his unemployed dad is also there
posts.label: He plays his dad mocking his videos
posts.take: He plays his own dad, in black and white, ranting about money, the engineering degree he skipped, and his “waahiyat” (rubbish) Instagram videos. Watching Anuj get told off isn’t why anyone follows Anuj.

posts.title: Layer room with mashups
posts.feeling: A pile of references, no single target.
posts.line: Shahid, Kareena, Central Cee, Modi, Hanumankind. Lots of names and no one to call out. Near the floor.

flow.beat: Clubhouse-style room UI, avatars, red arrow on Anuj.
A cappella singing of “Aaoge Jab Tum”; Shahid Kapoor and Kareena Kapoor cutouts appear; yellow lyric text.
Krish asks to rap over the singing; red arrow shifts to Krish.
Singing and rap overlap; Central Cee and Shahid/Kareena cutouts bounce; “How can I be homophobic? My b**** is gay” is shown.

Spoken dialogue about Instagram views, the page following him, Narendra Modi, Hanumankind, and a next-Vishal-Shekhar line; arrow moves between Nirav, Anuj, and Krish; Narendra Modi and Hanumankind cutouts appear.
Singing and fast rap overlap again; Shahid/Kareena and Hanumankind cutouts bounce; “Ten toes in…” and “Big Stepper” text appears.
Nirav and Anuj speak; Vishal Dadlani and Shekhar Ravjiani cutouts appear; “Vishal Shekhar is actually one guy” is shown.

posts.hook: Would y'all like to hear me sing?
posts.label: A Clubhouse room turns into a song mashup
posts.take: A fake Clubhouse room: one friend sings, another raps over it, and cutouts of Shahid, Kareena, Modi and Hanumankind keep popping up. Six jokes fighting for one reel. Nobody won.

posts.title: Zoom Through Sorrow
posts.feeling: Leave for glory, watch your old club win it.
posts.line: A fan’s grief, played straight in grayscale with no dialogue. It beat four straight but stopped at the middle.

flow.beat: Close-up profile of a man looking upward; white Real Madrid jersey graphic on chest; text reads “Mbappe watching PSG win back 2 back UCLs after going trophyless.”
Camera slowly zooms in; he blinks, looks down, then back up toward a wall-mounted light fixture.
Tight zoom on eye and cheek; he looks down again; cut to black and loop restart.

posts.hook: Mbappe watching PSG win back 2 back UCLs after going trophyless
posts.label: Mbappé watching PSG win without him
posts.take: A slow zoom on him in a Real Madrid shirt: “Mbappé watching PSG win back-to-back Champions Leagues” after leaving them. Football Twitter would love it; there’s no Anuj in it beyond his face.

posts.title: Glass-Review Parody
posts.feeling: “Reviewing glasses so I drink more water.”
posts.line: A bit about his own kitchen counter, carried by sad violins and Sarabhai inserts. Just below the middle.

flow.beat: Yellow overlay reads “Reviewing glasses so I drink more water”; Anuj introduces himself and says he is going to review glasses; sudden zoom on his mouth.
He holds a standard faceted glass, pours water into it, takes a sip, and describes it as versatile.
He shows a shorter faceted glass, pours water into it, compares the two heights, and the frame turns black-and-white with sad violin music.
He holds a heavy-bottomed whiskey glass, acts out a Bollywood father scene in black-and-white, then shows an elegant goblet glass with a split-screen insert of Sarabhai vs Sarabhai.
He drinks from the goblet glass, then shows a large beer mug and reacts negatively.
He holds a shot glass, tells a drunk auto-rickshaw story, flashes to black-and-white, then closes by saying “Bad, bad glass” while gesturing to throw it away.

posts.hook: What’s up guys, my name
named: Sad Violin (Sad Romance by Thao Nguyen Xanh)
posts.label: He reviews drinking glasses
posts.take: He reviews drinking glasses “so I drink more water”, with sad violins, a Bollywood dad bit and a Sarabhai vs Sarabhai cutaway. Funny inserts, 88 seconds about glasses.

posts.title: Swap and Style Jerseys
posts.feeling: No angle. The jerseys pose.
posts.line: Lotto x H&M jerseys, posed straight. No bluff to call and no feeling named, and it fell short of five straight.

flow.beat: Title card reads “LOTTO H&M” on black.
Rapid cuts show one man posing in red, black, and white Lotto jerseys under a dark spotlight.
Close-up shows round sunglasses, a smile, and a silver soccer ball pendant necklace.
In a parking garage, he does footwork tricks with a red soccer ball and spins it on his finger.
Multiple cloned versions of him stand in a line, then he kicks the ball at the camera.
On green turf, he wears a dark patterned jersey, dribbles, juggles, and poses.
On a rooftop, he wears a white pinstripe jersey, makes a finger-heart gesture, juggles the red ball, and looks at camera.
Final title card reads “LOTTO H&M.”

posts.hook: LOTTO H&M
posts.label: Sponsored Lotto x H&M jersey lookbook
posts.take: A sponsored Lotto x H&M jersey lookbook: ball tricks, rooftop poses, no joke. It looks great. His crowd came for jokes and scrolled. #38 of 40.

posts.title: Mock Complaint Loop
posts.feeling: “My parents don’t appreciate me.”
posts.line: Mom teases his self-praise until he says it’s going on Instagram. The camera turns on him again, and it lands in the bottom quarter again.

flow.beat: Black-and-white shot opens on a man in a grey tank top and silver chain; centered top text reads “my parents don't appreciate me.”
He talks toward someone off-camera; static low-angle frame shows a ceiling fan and wall light.
An off-camera female voice responds; he reacts with small smiles and looks around.
He argues back while the mother teases him about self-praise and “Instagram” is mentioned in the dialogue.
A woman briefly appears at the top left; he smiles, gives a thumbs-up, waves, points at the lens, and says the video is going on Instagram.

posts.hook: my parents don't appreciate me
posts.label: His mom mocks his self-praise
posts.take: “My parents don’t appreciate me.” His real mom, off camera, teases his self-praise until he announces it’s going on Instagram. Real banter, but once again Anuj is the one getting roasted.

posts.title: Profile-switch Storyline
posts.feeling: Rich friends and their “humble beginnings”.
posts.line: The rich friend’s hardship story collapses into his dad getting into racing. Right tribe, but solo in two profile shots, and it held the middle.

flow.beat: Left-facing profile; top text reads “when ur rich friend says they come from humble beginnings”; annoyed expression.
Right-facing profile; the man speaks fast and defensively about school, no food in the canteen, getting food from a dustbin, eating glass, and going to the hospital.
Left-facing profile interrupts with disbelief.
Right-facing profile continues, saying his dad begged colleagues, mentions racers, then says his dad got into racing.
Left-facing profile rolls eyes and shakes head; audio music fades in and swells.
Screen cuts to black while music continues.

posts.hook: when ur rich friend says they come from humble beginnings
posts.label: A rich friend’s “humble beginnings” story
posts.take: His rich friend explains his “humble beginnings”: no food in the canteen, dad begging colleagues for help… dad got into racing. A good target, played solo in two profile shots. Just missed.

posts.title: Reveal Car, Drive Off
posts.feeling: “Get used to these.” Sorry, not sorry.
posts.line: The BMW again, mocking its own flex. It beat ten straight and ended a run of bits about his own life.

flow.beat: A young man walks toward camera at night near a Blue Dart / DHL storefront, looking at his phone, then up, then adjusting his glasses.
Camera pans right to a matte black BMW sedan parked at an HP petrol pump.
Rear taillights, front headlight with blue ambient light, wide shot, and close-up of the M340i badge and rear taillight.
The man leans on the hood pointing at camera, then a quick interior shot shows the steering wheel and dashboard, then rear and front-angle shots of the car.
The man crosses his arms by the hood, and the car drives away into the night.

posts.hook: yall just have to get used to these for some time
posts.label: The BMW again: “get used to these”
posts.take: The BMW again, posed at a petrol pump: “y’all just have to get used to these for some time”. The eye-rolling caption carries it again; it beat the 10 reels before it and pulled a slow week back up.

posts.title: Say the tattoo
posts.feeling: The card doesn’t show the angle.
posts.line: One second of a forearm tattoo that says “Mauli”. Nothing to read an angle from. Near the floor.

flow.beat: Close-up handheld shot of a forearm with a cursive tattoo reading “Mauli” and a feather underneath; static lowercase on-screen text reads “mauli.”
A female voice says, “Oh my god, it says Mauli.”
Grey and pink patterned clothing and wooden flooring are visible in the background.

posts.hook: Oh my god, it says Mauli.
posts.label: A one-second shot of a tattoo that says “Mauli”
posts.take: A one-second clip of a forearm tattoo that says “Mauli”. Blink and it’s over, so people did.

posts.title: Stutter Into Chaos
posts.feeling: Hired to act, suddenly a writer.
posts.line: An industry tribe he knows, but it stays in a white room with no reveal. Below the middle.

flow.beat: Four actors stand in a white room with a clothing rack; three hold their hands up and one sits in an office chair.
The man in the black patterned robe steps forward and makes an intense face.
He pushes the seated man’s head, gets into the others’ faces, and the group restrains him through rapid close-up reaction cuts.
The group relaxes into a synchronized casual dancing pose and the video loops.

posts.hook: comics when they get hired to act but suddenly have writing inputs
posts.label: Comic actors who suddenly have “writing inputs”
posts.take: “Comics when they get hired to act but suddenly have writing inputs”: one actor loses it, the others hold him back. An industry in-joke with no reveal at the end.

posts.title: Sundae Taste Tour
posts.feeling: No angle. A favourite place, shown.
posts.line: Baskin Robbins with a friend. It landed well, but there’s no viewpoint in it. The city is just where it happens.

flow.beat: Two men wearing sunglasses sit at a wooden table inside Baskin Robbins, holding up ice cream cones; on-screen text reads “We’re in Mumbai” and “And our favorite ice cream place in the whole wide world.”
A gloved hand scoops green ice cream, then a chocolate-rimmed waffle cone with white ice cream appears, followed by the man in the white shirt eating a spoonful.
The two men pose with cones, a yellow-striped vehicle exterior appears briefly, then the store interior, a cone close-up, and the Baskin Robbins storefront appear.
Three plated desserts appear, the man in the white shirt tastes a sundae, the man in the pink shirt eats a sundae, and the man in the white shirt presents a tiramisu sundae while speaking to camera.

posts.hook: We’re in Mumbai
posts.label: Tasting sundaes at Baskin Robbins
posts.take: He and a friend at Baskin Robbins in Mumbai tasting a Dubai chocolate sundae. Zero jokes, still his top third. People like hanging out with him, not just laughing at him.

posts.title: Open with chord
posts.feeling: No angle. A piano take.
posts.line: A 14-second piano take with no joke. It fell short of twelve straight.

flow.beat: The pianist sits at a grand piano with hands poised over the keys.
He strikes a heavy opening chord, lifts his right hand, and runs downward fast.
He plays rapid arpeggios; the key movement mirrors in the red piano lid.
He shifts into rhythmic chords and the video cuts off mid-performance.

posts.hook: fresh_res
posts.label: A 14-second piano performance
posts.take: A 14-second piano performance. Lovely. Not what anyone came for. #39 of 40.

posts.title: Roast by voiceover
posts.feeling: Delhi’s obsession is loud.
posts.line: A Delhi voice roasts him. Pointed at another city again, and again the middle.

flow.beat: close-up selfie of a young man in the driver’s seat wearing red-tinted sunglasses, a silver chain, and a grey t-shirt; he speaks to camera.
an off-camera male voice shouts in Hindi with local slang and profanity; the driver turns slightly and smirks.
visible text reads “watching obsession: Delhi”.

posts.hook: watching obsession: Delhi
posts.label: A Delhi voice roasts him from off camera
posts.take: “Watching Obsession: Delhi”: a loud Delhi voice roasts him from the back seat. Delhi-vs-Mumbai again, and again just short.

posts.title: Escalate a complaint
posts.feeling: “It’s rigged. Rigged for Messi.”
posts.line: He is the fan who takes losing personally, already rehearsing the next excuse. Solo, and it beat sixteen straight.

flow.beat: Speaker looks down, shakes his head, and mutters; on-screen text reads “practicing for when Ronaldo loses yet another WC.”
He puts hands on hips, looks off-camera left, and continues complaining.
He turns right, gestures, and becomes more animated and defensive.
He leans closer to the camera, gestures mockingly, and says the competition is “rigged,” “Rigged for Messi to win,” and “FIFA’s boy.”

posts.hook: It’s rigged.
posts.label: A rant that Ronaldo’s losses are “rigged for Messi”
posts.take: “Practicing for when Ronaldo loses yet another World Cup”: it’s rigged, it’s for Messi, he’s FIFA’s boy. Fan grief everyone has heard from that one friend, timed to football season. It beat the 16 reels before it.

posts.title: Mock-phone rant
posts.feeling: ₹248 crore for 750 metres of flyover.
posts.line: A real Mumbai grievance, but delivered as a rant. He is amused by his city, not angry at it, and the anger didn’t land.

flow.beat: Man speaks to camera in black-and-white, gestures, and visible text names the Mrinal Tai Gore flyover, 248 crores, 750 meters, and “unfinished.”
He holds a white plaster bust to his ear as a mock phone, the dialogue turns into a louder caller voice, and the visible text shows the aggressive exchange ending with “dumbass.”

posts.hook: POV: 248cr for a 750m flyover (unfinished)
posts.label: A rant about a ₹248 crore unfinished flyover
posts.take: ₹248 crore for a 750-metre flyover that’s still unfinished, ranted into a plaster bust like it’s a phone. The anger is real and the issue is real, but he’s angry here, not funny.

posts.title: Food Tour Cuts
posts.feeling: No angle. A restaurant, shown.
posts.line: O Pedro with friends. It landed in the top quarter, but the reader can’t credit a viewpoint. It’s hosting, not insight.

flow.beat: Three people sit at a booth; the center man holds a burger and fries.
Close-ups show prawns emptied from a green coconut shell and chocolate sauce poured over a tart.
The center man takes a bite of a folded taco; the three diners smile and pose with the burger plate while “O Pedro baby!” is spoken.
Quick cuts show the restaurant interior, tables, and a large wall mirror.
The coconut prawn dish and a wide dining-room shot with hanging plants appear.
A Burrata salad appears as the woman speaks directly to camera.

posts.hook: We're in Mumbai at what people say is one of
posts.label: Eating at O Pedro with friends
posts.take: Three friends at O Pedro, a Goan restaurant in Mumbai: coconut prawns, burrata, a shouted “O Pedro baby!”. No joke, all vibe, and it made his top 20%.

posts.title: Freeze-Frame Reveal
posts.feeling: “Anuj’s PA.” Correction: not Anuj’s PA.
posts.line: Broadway’s launch arrives through a staged fight and a PA who isn’t his. The brand bought his self-deflating angle. Upper half.

flow.beat: Two men in orange shirts face a man in a white turban in a retail store; shouting, bleeps, and fast cuts continue.
A woman in a black dress walks through the store, gestures at shoppers, and speaks to camera.
She falls backward into a chair in slow motion; the text shows “Aysha Sultan,” “Anuj’s PA,” then “Not Anuj’s PA,” with a record scratch and “Yup, that’s me…” line.
Cut to an exterior black building with a viewfinder overlay reading “3 DAYS BEFORE THE LAUNCH.”

posts.hook: What the f*#^ are y'all doing here?
posts.label: Broadway store launch ad: “not Anuj’s PA”
posts.take: A Broadway store-launch teaser: a shouting match in the store, a woman introduced as “Anuj’s PA”, a record scratch, “Not Anuj’s PA”. A brand deal with an actual joke in it, and it held his top half.

posts.title: Sock Mistake Cut
posts.pokes: The friend who used a sock
posts.feeling: That one disgusting thing your friend did.
posts.line: His crew being idiots, filmed like an inside joke. No names, no message. It beat twenty straight.

flow.beat: A man lies on a blue sofa; another man removes a white sock from his foot and hands it to a woman.
The woman takes the sock, mistakes it for a tissue, and blows her nose into it.
Cut to a man in a black shirt leaning over an office desk and speaking urgently.
The woman realizes it was a sock, screams in disgust, and throws it away; an office phone rings in the background.

posts.hook: Oh thank you.
posts.label: Office prank: a friend’s sock used as a tissue
posts.take: The office crew: one friend pulls off his sock, another takes it for a tissue and blows her nose in it. Gross, quick, and very “this happened in our office”. Top 10%, and it beat the 20 reels before it.

posts.title: Reframe with punchline
posts.feeling: Being in a bad place has a postcode.
posts.line: Every Mumbaikar has been stuck in Andheri East. He laughs at his own city from inside it. It didn’t beat the sock reel before it, but that one was top 10%: strong company.

flow.beat: Close-up of a young man holding a phone to his ear.
Quick cuts show a face modified by a female appearance filter speaking to camera.
Cut back to the man; he looks down, then says, “Damn. Andheri East.”

posts.hook: in a bad place rn
posts.label: “I’m in a bad place” → “Andheri East”
posts.take: Five seconds. “I’m in a bad place right now.” “Damn. Andheri East.” Every Mumbaikar has been stuck there. Top 15%; only the sock prank right before it did better.

posts.title: Taunt into play
posts.feeling: Talk big, slide into the net.
posts.line: His crew on the turf, the trash talk undone by the slide into the net. Top quarter.

flow.beat: Young man in white jersey does a wide squat taunt in front of the goal; bright yellow text reads “SUCK MY FAT C***K”; spoken line starts “Suck my fat...”.
Tall man in sunglasses stretches on the turf; shorter man in black stands with arms crossed.
A ball is kicked toward the goal; the man in white slides feet-first into the back of the net; off-camera voice says “Easy, easy.”
The man in white gets up, runs across the turf, and bumps into the man in sunglasses.
Goalkeeper in grey stands ready in the goal with a ball on the turf in front.

posts.hook: Suck my fat...
posts.label: Football trash talk, then he slides into the net
posts.take: Turf football with the boys: big trash talk, then he slides feet-first into the net. The crew does the heavy lifting again.

posts.title: Cut to Ludo
posts.feeling: Every “urgent pitch” is a board game.
posts.line: The serious huddle turns out to be a Ludo game. His own work world, called out by people inside it. Top 20%.

flow.beat: Extreme low-angle shot of four people in corporate attire standing in a tight circle and talking seriously.
Wide shot reveals a modern office lounge with a wooden coffee table and a Ludo board game.
Close-up shows a white die rolling on the board and landing on two.
Wide shot shows the group slumping and sitting down on blue sofas.
Medium shot shows a man in a peach shirt speaking and gesturing.

posts.hook: humari pitch mein
posts.label: A tense office “pitch” is actually a Ludo game
posts.take: Four people in office clothes huddle over “our pitch”… it’s a Ludo game. He tagged half a creative agency’s worth of friends, and they showed up.

posts.title: Flip State Punchline
posts.feeling: A pun, not a feeling.
posts.line: The Andheri joke’s twin, pointed at UP. No Mumbaikar feeling behind it, just a double meaning on “state”. It fell short of all nine posts before it.

flow.beat: First character in a green t-shirt smiles and asks, “Are Saurabh long time no see, what's up man? What's up bro”.
Cut to the same actor as a second character with silver metallic sunglasses and a mustache filter; he says, “nothing bro, I'm just in a really bad state right now. Um...”
Cut back to the first character looking down, then up, and saying “UP.”

posts.hook: in a bad state rn
posts.label: “I’m in a bad state” → “UP”
posts.take: The Andheri joke’s twin: “I’m in a bad state” → “UP”. A pun on a state, not a feeling anyone in Mumbai has. All 9 reels before it did better.

twins.line: Same setup, same five-second two-hander, one word apart. Andheri East is a Mumbaikar laughing at his own city. UP is a pun about someone else’s home.
Both show off a possession. The BMW heckles itself. The jerseys just pose.
Both are paid. Blinkit bought his angle on creators. Startup Village bought a panel format.
Same solo performer. In one he calls out the industry. In the other, his dad calls him out.

feeders.source: Ranks and postcards from the SIM-W03 run packet. Order inside each week is approximate.

series.name: Roasting his own industry
series.what: He plays people from his own industry: Parle’s marketing team milking the “Melodi” meme, creators who think one viral reel is an “IP”, an agency pitch huddle that turns out to be Ludo, comics with “writing inputs”.
series.verdict: His most reliable thing. 3 of 4 landed in the top 20%. The miss (comics with “writing inputs”) stays in one white room and never has a reveal.
series.sub: He plays marketers, creators and agency people
series.take: Anuj is a creator who works with brands, so he roasts creators and brand people from the inside: Parle’s marketing team milking the Melodi meme, creators who hit 10M once and start saying “IP”, an urgent pitch that’s a Ludo game. Half his crowd works in this world. 3 of 4 made his top quarter; the miss (actors who suddenly have “writing inputs”) never lands a reveal.
series.say: His surest hit. He plays the marketing team, the one-viral-reel creator and the agency bros, and a lot of his crowd works with exactly these people. 3 of 4 made his top 20%; the miss (actors with “writing inputs”) never gets its reveal.

series.name: Football heartbreak
series.what: Football told as a fan’s wound: Ronaldo’s loss is “rigged for Messi”, Mbappé watches PSG win twice, a turf taunt that ends with him sliding into the net.
series.verdict: 2 of 3 in the top 25%. It works when he plays the hurt, over-invested fan.
series.take: Football as personal grief: Ronaldo “robbed” by FIFA, Mbappé watching PSG win without him, trash talk on the turf that ends with him in the net. 2 of 3 made his top quarter. It works when he’s the wounded fan; the sponsored jersey lookbook is football too, and it came #38 of 40.
series.say: He plays the fan who took it way too personally. Ronaldo being “rigged for Messi” hit top 13%, the turf slide top 25%. Mbappé watching PSG win held the middle.

series.name: The crew being idiots
series.what: Sketches with his friends where something dumb happens: a sock used as a tissue in the office, SoBo kids panicking outside Bombay, a Clubhouse-style room that falls apart.
series.verdict: Two hits and one flop. The sock prank (top 10%) and the SoBo panic (top 28%) each have one clear joke. The Clubhouse mashup piles up references and landed near the bottom.
series.take: His friends doing dumb things: the sock-for-a-tissue office prank, South Bombay kids panicking outside their bubble, a Clubhouse room falling apart. The sock prank beat the 20 reels before it. The Clubhouse one crammed six celebrities and a rap verse into one joke and sank.
series.say: One dumb thing his friends do, and it flies: the sock-as-a-tissue prank beat every reel in the 20 before it. When it piles on references, like the Clubhouse mashup, it sinks.

series.name: The BMW (pre-roasted)
series.what: His matte black BMW M340i, always posted with a caption that mocks the flex first: “we get it bro”, then “yall just have to get used to these”.
series.verdict: Both landed in the upper third. The second one beat 10 posts in a row.
series.sub: His BMW, always mocked in the caption
series.take: He bought a matte-black BMW M340i and keeps posting it, always with a caption that rolls its eyes first: “we get it bro”, then “y’all just have to get used to these”. That eye-roll is the trick. Both landed in his top third.
series.say: He never just shows off the car. The caption roasts it first (“we get it bro”, “get used to these”), and both posts landed in his top 30%.

series.name: Eating out with friends
series.what: Him and friends at a Mumbai restaurant naming dishes: O Pedro (coconut prawns, burrata), Baskin Robbins (Dubai chocolate sundae).
series.verdict: Both landed well (top 20% and top 32%). There’s no joke in them; this is a separate lifestyle lane from the comedy.
series.sub: Eating out in Mumbai with friends
series.take: Eating out in Mumbai with friends: O Pedro, Baskin Robbins. Not a single joke, and both still landed in his top third. His crowd likes hanging out with him, not just laughing at him.
series.say: No joke, just eating out with friends, and it still works: O Pedro top 20%, Baskin Robbins top 33%. A lifestyle lane that sits next to the comedy.

series.name: 5-second place puns
series.what: New in run 4. A 5–7 second two-hander where a vague line ends on a place name: “I’m in a bad place” → “Andheri East”, “I’m in a bad state” → “UP”.
series.verdict: Tried twice in one week with opposite results: Andheri East top 15%, UP top 88%. Andheri East is a commute every Mumbaikar has suffered. UP is only a word pun.
series.sub: 5-second jokes that end on a place name
series.take: New in run 4: five-second jokes that end on a place name. “Bad place” → Andheri East made his top 15%. “Bad state” → UP sank to #35. Andheri East is a commute every Mumbaikar has suffered; UP is just wordplay. One more try will tell us whether this is a format or a fluke.
series.say: Same 5-second setup, opposite results. “Bad place → Andheri East” is a commute every Mumbaikar has suffered: top 15%. “Bad state → UP” is just a pun: top 88%.

series.name: Loose on the street
series.what: He walks up to real people: mediates a roadside crash with a forced hug, lies to a parking attendant about a driver who doesn’t exist, hosts street rap battles and roasts.
series.verdict: The steadiest thing he posts: all 4 landed between top 35% and top 50%. Never a hit, never a flop.
series.take: Anuj with real strangers: forcing a hug at a road fight, lying to a parking attendant about a driver who doesn’t exist, hosting rap battles and roasts. All four in his top half, none in the top quarter. The strangers are gold; the reels run a minute too long.
series.say: Unscripted bits with randoms. Always fine, never a hit: all four sat between top 35% and top 50%.

series.name: Delhi vs Mumbai
series.what: Mumbai shrugs while Delhi panics at an alarm, a Delhi voice roasting him, a rant about ₹248 crore spent on 750 m of unfinished flyover.
series.verdict: Middle to low (top 42% to 75%). Comparing cities lands worse than jokes from inside Mumbai.
series.sub: Delhi vs Mumbai and city complaints
series.take: City jabs: Mumbai shrugs while Delhi panics at an alarm, a Delhi voice roasting him, a rant about a ₹248 crore flyover. The alarm one held his top half; the other two sank below it. City stereotypes are middle-of-the-pack at best for him.
series.say: Comparing cities lands worse than joking from inside Mumbai. The flyover rant was angry, not funny: top 75%.

series.name: Brand deals
series.what: Paid posts: Blinkit (an AI replaces him as the son, for Mother’s Day), Broadway’s Bandra launch, District (an MJ mix-up), Lotto x H&M jerseys, a Startup Village rapid-fire panel.
series.verdict: The widest spread in the account: #1 and #40 are both brand deals. When the brand is written into one of his sketches (Blinkit, Broadway) it lands. When it brings its own format (a jersey lookbook, a panel Q&A) it lands last.
series.take: Five sponsored reels and the widest spread in the feed: #1 and #40. Blinkit wrote him into a Mother’s Day story where an AI replaces him as the son: #1 of 40. Broadway gave him a scene (“Not Anuj’s PA”). Lotto x H&M (a lookbook) and Startup Village (a panel Q&A) gave him a format with no joke, and his crowd scrolled. Hire the bit, not the face.
series.say: His widest swing. When the brand is written into his sketch, it lands: Blinkit was his #1 post. When the brand brings its own format (a panel, a jersey lookbook), it sinks to the very bottom.

series.name: Playing both sides
series.what: He plays both sides of a conversation with jump cuts: flatmates deciding to move in, girls’ vs boys’ life updates, the rich friend’s “humble beginnings”.
series.verdict: Middle to low (top 52% to 80%). The two-character format on its own doesn’t carry a post; it needs a sharp target.
series.sub: He plays both people in a conversation
series.take: He plays both people in a conversation with jump cuts: flatmates moving in, girls’ vs boys’ life updates, the rich friend’s “humble beginnings”. All three in his bottom half. The format doesn’t carry anything on its own.
series.say: Him playing both people in a chat. Without a sharp target it just sits there: all three in his bottom half.

series.name: Just Anuj, about Anuj
series.what: Just him and his own life: waking at 2 PM to the emergency alert, a backseat story, handing cash to a worker, reviewing water glasses, a tattoo, a piano take.
series.verdict: His weakest recurring thing by volume: 6 posts, none above top 55%.
series.sub: Just him, about his own day
series.take: Just him and his own day: sleeping through the emergency alert, reviewing drinking glasses, a tattoo, a piano take, cash for a scaffolding worker. Six reels, none made his top half. Without someone to roast, there’s nothing to send to the group chat.
series.say: Just Anuj, about Anuj: sleeping through the alarm, reviewing glasses, a piano take. Six tries, none above his middle.

series.name: Getting told off at home
series.what: Monologues where someone at home judges his Instagram life: a friend says scrolling reels isn’t a job, his mom mocks his self-praise, he plays his dad calling his videos “waahiyat”.
series.verdict: All 3 landed in the bottom quarter. When he’s the one being judged, it doesn’t land.
series.take: Somebody at home tells Anuj off: his dad (played by him, in black and white) calls his videos “waahiyat”, his mom teases his self-praise, a friend says reels aren’t a job. His crowd follows him to watch him roast everyone else. Flip it and they keep scrolling: all three in his bottom quarter.
series.say: When he’s the one being roasted (his dad on his videos, his mom on his ego, a friend saying reels aren’t a job), his crowd scrolls. All three in his bottom quarter.

1.head: A Blinkit ad became his best post
1.body: Blinkit’s Mother’s Day ad, where his mom swaps him for an AI assistant, ranked #1 of all 40 posts. A sketch about creators who think one viral video makes them an “IP” ranked #3. His new BMW debuted with the caption “we get it bro” and landed in his top 25%. Solo bits about his own day (sleeping through the emergency alert, a friend’s lecture that reels aren’t a job) landed in his bottom half.

2.head: A Parle parody hit #2; a sponsored panel hit #40
2.body: His parody of Parle’s marketing team milking the “Melodi” meme beat each of the 9 posts before it and ranked #2. Street bits with strangers (a made-up driver, a rap battle at a cosmetics stall, a bathrobe roast) all landed mid-table. A sponsored Startup Village rapid-fire panel ranked #40, below every post before it.

3.head: Seven of ten sank; the BMW sequel saved it
3.body: Mostly him alone: reviewing drinking glasses, his mom mocking his self-praise, a tattoo, a piano take. Seven of ten landed in his bottom half. The second BMW post (“get used to these”) beat each of the 10 posts before it. A sponsored Lotto x H&M jersey lookbook ranked #38.

4.head: His friend-group sketches carried the run
4.body: Six of ten landed in his top 25%. Best: an office prank where a friend’s sock gets used as a tissue, which beat each of the 20 posts before it. A rant that Ronaldo’s losses are “rigged for Messi” beat 16. He tried a new 5-second joke twice: “I’m in a bad place” → “Andheri East” landed in his top 15%; “I’m in a bad state” → “UP” landed in his bottom 15%.

read.label: Works best
read.text: Parodies of his own industry: Parle’s marketers, creators after one viral video, a “pitch” that’s a Ludo game. 3 of 4 landed in his top 20%.

read.label: Works least
read.text: Family judging his Instagram career: his dad calls his videos “waahiyat”, his mom mocks his self-praise, a friend says reels aren’t a job. All 3 landed in his bottom quarter.

read.label: Watch next
read.text: The new 5-second place-name joke. Andheri East (a commute every Mumbaikar knows) landed top 15%; UP (just a pun) landed bottom 15%.

feeders.dateNote: Dates are approximate (from each card’s age), anchored so the Mother’s Day post lands on May 8.

all.head: His crowd comes to watch him roast everyone else.
all.body: His own industry, his BMW, his city. They show up hardest when his friends are in it, and keep scrolling when he’s alone, preachy, or the one getting told off.

1.head: A Blinkit ad hit #1; his solo bits sank
1.body: Blinkit’s Mother’s Day ad, where his mom swaps him for an AI assistant because he’s “too busy being an influencer”, was his best post in 90 days. The sketch about creators who start saying “IP” after one viral reel (with Ruhee Dosani) made top 8%, and the BMW debut, roasted in its own caption (“we get it bro”), top 23%. Everything where he’s alone or being lectured sank to his bottom half: sleeping through the emergency alert, retelling a night, a friend saying reels aren’t a job, two flatmates trading confessions.

2.head: A Parle parody hit #2; a paid panel came last
2.body: His parody of Parle’s marketing team milking the “Melodi” meme, played in a Versace robe, was his #2 post in 90 days (top 5%). Street bits with strangers held the middle without breaking out: a rap battle at a cosmetics stall (top 40%), blaming a parking mess on a made-up driver (45%), a street-mic roast in a bathrobe (50%). The sponsored Startup Village rapid-fire panel came last of all 40, and his dad mocking his videos (85%) and the Clubhouse song mashup (90%) were near the bottom too.

3.head: Seven of ten sank; the BMW sequel led
3.body: Mostly Anuj on his own: reviewing drinking glasses to sad violins, his mom mocking his self-praise, a one-second tattoo shot, a 14-second piano take. Seven of ten landed in his bottom half. The second BMW post (“get used to these”) was the run’s best at top 30%, beating the 10 posts before it, with Baskin Robbins with friends close behind (33%). The sponsored Lotto x H&M jersey lookbook came 38th of 40.

4.head: 6 of 10 in his top 25%: crew, food, football
4.body: His best run: six of ten in his top quarter, four of them with his people in the frame. The office crew’s sock-as-a-tissue prank (top 10%) beat the 20 posts before it; the Ludo “pitch” (18%), O Pedro with friends (20%) and the turf trash-talk slide (25%) followed, plus a rant that Ronaldo’s losses are “rigged for Messi” (13%). He tried a new 5-second format twice: “bad place → Andheri East” hit top 15%, “bad state → UP” sank to 88%.

drivers.idea: Most of his feed lives or dies on the idea. Roasting a world he’s part of (creators, his BMW, Andheri East) lands. Being the one roasted (dad, mom, a lecture) or having no joke at all (piano, a lookbook) gets scrolled past.
drivers.moment: Five reels rode something already in the air: Mother’s Day (Blinkit), the Melodi meme (Parle), Ronaldo vs Messi, Mbappé leaving PSG, a flyover scandal. Three made his top quarter, including #1 and #2. The moment opens the door; the bit still has to walk through. The flyover rant was angry, not funny, and stalled.
drivers.faces: Put him with people and the floor rises: the office crew (sock, Ludo), the turf boys, strangers on the street, friends at a restaurant. All nine landed in his top half and four made the top quarter. None of them sank to the bottom half.
drivers.craft: Five reels lost on execution, not the idea: too long (a 90-second parking lie, 88 seconds about glasses), too short (a one-second tattoo), too busy (the Clubhouse mashup), or the brand hiding on the end card. None made the top quarter.

feeders.primer: Anuj (@anuj.mp4) is a Mumbai comedy creator: crew sketches, street bits with strangers, a BMW he can’t stop roasting himself about, and the odd brand deal. 40 reels since May 1, ranked against each other at day 7.

repeats.name: The Versace robe
repeats.say: His go-to costume. It sold the Parle marketing boss (top 5%), but the street-mic host and the “writing inputs” actor wore it too and sat mid-feed. The robe dresses a bit; it doesn’t carry one.

repeats.name: The matte black BMW
repeats.say: On camera twice, both in his top 30%. It works because he mocks the flex before anyone else can.

repeats.name: His mom
repeats.say: Same co-star, opposite results. Mom swapping him for an AI in Blinkit’s ad was his #1 post. Mom mocking his self-praise sank to top 78%. Who gets roasted decides it.

repeats.name: The office
repeats.say: Two sketches at the office desks with the crew: the sock prank (top 10%) and the Ludo “pitch” (top 18%). Both hit.

repeats.name: The turf
repeats.say: Same turf, two different posts. His own trash-talk slide made top 25%; the sponsored Lotto x H&M jersey lookbook came 38th of 40.

repeats.name: The piano
repeats.say: As a prop in the Parle sketch: top 5%. As the whole post (a 14-second piano take): top 98%.

repeats.name: His sunglasses
repeats.say: In eight posts and they change nothing: they’re spread from top 25% to top 95%. A look, not a hook.

3.head: Sketches aimed at a world his crowd already knows
3.what: Three scripted sketches where he plays someone: the influencer son his mom swaps for an AI in Blinkit’s Mother’s Day ad, Parle’s marketing boss milking the “Melodi” meme, and creators who start saying “IP” after one viral reel. Plus the office crew’s sock-as-a-tissue prank.
3.why: Each one rides something his followers already live with: Mother’s Day, a meme everyone was sharing, creator culture, office life. The joke lands on someone else, or on him but delivered by someone else (his mom). One clear idea per post.

2.head: His people and his running jokes
2.what: The office Ludo “pitch” and the turf trash-talk slide with his crew, eating out at O Pedro with friends, the BMW debut he roasts in his own caption, a rant that Ronaldo’s losses are “rigged for Messi”, and the 5-second “bad place → Andheri East” pun.
2.why: His followers are already in on these: the same friends, the same car joke, the same Mumbai. Football works when he plays the over-invested fan; the pun works because Andheri East is a commute his whole crowd has suffered.

1.head: Easy to like, not much to share
1.what: Unscripted bits with strangers (a forced hug at a roadside crash, a rap battle at a cosmetics stall, blaming a made-up driver, a street roast in a bathrobe), the second BMW post, Baskin Robbins with friends, the Broadway store ad written into his life, South Bombay kids lost outside their bubble, Delhi vs Mumbai, and Mbappé watching PSG win.
1.why: They hold his top half but never break out. Fun to watch once, with nothing that makes people send them on: the strangers aren’t characters his crowd knows, and the city and football takes read more like news than a bit.

0.head: Him alone, him being judged, or someone else’s format
0.what: Solo days (sleeping through the emergency alert, reviewing drinking glasses, a one-second tattoo, a 14-second piano take, retelling a night), being told off (his dad on his videos, his mom on his ego, a friend saying reels aren’t a job), two-person chats where he plays both sides, and brand formats he didn’t write (the District ad, the Lotto x H&M lookbook, the Startup Village panel in last place).
0.why: There’s no one else in the frame to roast, or he’s the one being roasted. Puns without a shared experience (“bad state → UP”) and posts that pile on references (the Clubhouse mashup) sink here too.
